==Problem==

How many whole numbers between 99 and 999 contain exactly one 0?

<math> \text{(A)}\ 72\qquad\text{(B)}\ 90\qquad\text{(C)}\ 144\qquad\text{(D)}\ 162\qquad\text{(E)}\ 180 </math>

==Solution 1==
Numbers with exactly one zero have the form <math>\overline{a0b}</math> or <math>\overline{ab0}</math>, where the <math>a,b \neq 0</math>. There are <math>(9\cdot1\cdot9)+(9\cdot9\cdot1) = 81+81 = \boxed{162}</math> such numbers, hence our answer is <math>\fbox{D}</math>.

==Solution 2 (Complementary Counting)==
(Whole numbers between 99 and 999)-(Whole numbers which do not contain exactly one 0)= (How many whole numbers between 99 and 999 contain exactly one 0).

<math>1)</math> How many whole numbers are between 99 and 999, <math>999-99=900</math>, so there are 900 numbers between 99 and 999.

<math>2a)</math> How many whole numbers in this range do not contain the digit <math>0</math>, there are <math>10-1=9</math> possible digits for each digit in this three digit number, <math>9^3=729</math>. So there are <math>729</math> numbers in this range which do not contain the digit <math>0</math>.

<math>2b)</math> How many whole numbers in this range contain the digit <math>0</math> 2 times, there are <math>10-1=9</math> possible digits for the first digit and the other two digits have to be the digit <math>0</math>. So there are <math>9</math> of these numbers. 

So there are <math>900-(729+9)</math> whole numbers between 99 and 999 that contain exactly one 0.

Simplifying the expression we get that there are <math>162</math> whole numbers between 99 and 999 that contain exactly one 0. So the answer is <math>\fbox{D}</math>.
